result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A is about 93 words, friendly and easy to paste. Its main weaknesses are that `space-4` names a scale step rather than a purpose and it never says to reuse the closest token when one only nearly fits. B states the purpose-over-appearance rule better and adds a clear 'second real use case' test, but it has preamble and word-count commentary around the message, a bracketed [Owner] that must be filled in before posting, and a slightly sterner tone. Neither answer tells people to reuse the closest existing token; both only say to use one if it already fits. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A has the stronger substance. However, A wraps the message in a preamble and a word-count note, and it leaves an [Owner] placeholder inside the message. B is warmer and closer to paste-ready, but its space-4 example breaks the purpose-based rule, and it has no test for whether a new token is justified.
